campaign: KACP-stack runtime 3-arm — inline+KACP+canonicalize vs launch-noalias vs full package
question: Does the KACP stack (host-wrapper inlining + kernel-arg constant propagation + canonicalize) produce a device-side runtime benefit on PolyBench/GPU — alone (A vs B) and on top of the launch-noalias pass (B vs C)?

pins.llvm: b21a0cb9ddee (gsoc/aa-launch-noalias; detached checkout on the box)
pins.corpus: f5613c4 (experiment/static-kernels-pr25 — static kernels, closed-world favorable case)
pins.machine: Lambda A10 24GB us-east-1, Ubuntu 22.04.5, CUDA 12.8, driver 570.148.08
pins.protocol: 3 warmup + 8 timed, serialized -j1 via --accurate-mode, validation on (42/42 v/CIR + v/CIR-merge per arm)

A_control.note: stamp reconstructed verbatim from on-disk run output; the original publish hung on GitHub SSH host-key verification (fresh box had no known_hosts) before creating the stamp

result.convention: S(X;Y) = tX/tY; >1 means Y faster than X
result.verdict: The KACP stack is RUNTIME-NEUTRAL on this corpus despite a ~25-30% instruction reduction: B-vs-A geomean 1.0005, all significant per-bench CIs within +/-1% except gramschmidt (0.971, small regression) and lu (0.995). The full package's 1.61x is entirely the launch-noalias pass; it reproduces the Sep-12 campaign (1.6722x) within run-to-run band.

ci95.S_A_B: 8/21 significant: gramschmidt 0.971 [0.970,0.971] (only >1% move, a regression), lu 0.995 [0.992,0.999]; the rest of the significant set <=+/-1% (atax 1.003, bicg 1.005, covariance 0.998, gesummv 1.009, mvt 1.001, syrk 1.001); 13 crossing 1
ci95.S_B_C: 15/21 entirely above 1; 0 below; 6 crossing (convolution-2d, convolution-3d, fdtd-2d, jacobi-1d-imper, jacobi-2d-imper, lu)

local_full_corpus_A_to_B.source: kacp-fullscan/tool_scan.md (tool-based scan through cir-offload-merge, local lowering, all 21 benchmarks)

sass_box_binaries_7bench_subset.regression: convolution-3d kernel 104 -> 128 (+24) — matches the local PTX +13 anomaly

instruction_axis.interpretation: The corpus is memory-bound; eliminating address/launch-arg computation does not move wall time. Instruction-count metrics are not predictive of runtime here — the noalias pass wins by changing memory access behavior, not by removing instructions.
